text: {"score":2,"justification":"The core numbers match the card (11.4%, 3.6%, 7.57, z 1.06, 45 documented claims, 19 99215 documented, 1 below billed, 4 of 32). The \"7\" the script could not match is the 7% data share, which is not on the card and is likely from a tool output, so it is minor. But several narrative claims are contradicted by the card and the argument is internally muddled. The summary says the rate is \"roughly double the all-provider rate in every chronic-condition band\": the bands show 2.2x, 2.1x, 1.9x, 2.0x, 2.1x and 1.35x for 5+, so the 5+ band is not double. It says the sampled low-complexity claims \"include visits coded only for acute, usually simple problems such as upper respiratory infection, UTI, rash or follow-up\", which is partly supported (J06.9, N39.0, R21, Z09), but \"follow-up\" for Z09 is loose. It says \"repeated time entries appear\", but nothing in the card supports this. The \"17% for comparison providers\" figure is the all-provider rate and is okay. C0013071 is cited as flagged on the problems element, but the card has no per-claim note flags, so this is unsupported. The headline says \"at every complexity level\", which overstates. The inference of \"cloned or inflated documentation\" is speculative. The next steps are concrete but generic, and the cited claims in the examples are fine.
